final_message:
I calibrated all seven joint offsets and wrote them to `params.json`. With these values the simulation matches all 12 reference photos (4 poses × 3 cameras) to within the photos' own noise.

| Parameter | Value (rad) |
|---|---|
| offset_1 | 0.1437 |
| offset_2 | -0.1768 |
| offset_3 | 0.2231 |
| offset_4 | 0.1572 |
| offset_5 | -0.2420 |
| offset_6 | 0.2046 |
| offset_7 | -0.2964 |

**Method**
- **Scene:** the task code sets each joint angle to the commanded value plus its offset and computes the pose directly; nothing is simulated over time. So the only unknowns are the 7 offsets.
- **Loss:** the difference between rendered and reference pixels, averaged over all 12 photos at once. Fitting every pose together is what separates the offsets of joints whose effects look alike in any single pose (for example joints 1 and 3).
- **Search:** first a coarse joint-by-joint grid sweep over the full ±0.4 rad range on heavily blurred images, then a finer joint-by-joint refinement. Last, two runs of a standard simplex optimizer (Nelder-Mead) on lightly blurred images, which lowered the loss from about 14 to 0.22.

**Result**
- The remaining per-image error (5.0–6.5) equals the variance of the stated sensor noise (2.5² ≈ 6.25) in every photo. That means no systematic pose error is left, and all four poses fit about equally well.
- The built-in comparison tool shows a 0.0% mismatch fraction; its mean absolute difference is about 1.85/255.

Because the offsets fit four quite different poses equally well, I expect them to carry over to the held-out poses rather than being fitted to pixels of the training photos.
